children: xStocks has surpassed $800 million in assets backing its tokenised stocks and ETFs, while the number of unique holders has exceeded 300,000, according to figures released by the company.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The network now covers 715 tokenised instruments across ten blockchains and reports more than $40 billion in cumulative transaction volume.
Each xStock representing a listed stock or ETF is backed 1:1 by the corresponding underlying security, which is held in regulated custody, according to the project’s website.

The tokens can be transferred and traded onchain, giving holders economic exposure to changes in the underlying asset’s value. xStocks says the instruments can be redeemed for the equivalent cash value or the underlying security, subject to the relevant terms and eligibility requirements.
The $40 billion figure represents cumulative transaction activity, rather than the value of assets currently backing the tokens or an equivalent amount of new investor money.

Comparable xStocks figures have counted centralised and decentralised exchange activity, as well as minting and redemptions. Distribution has expanded through more than 100 integrations covering exchanges, self-custodial wallets, decentralised exchanges and lending markets.

Users can hold, transfer or swap the tokens and, if supported by a third-party protocol, use them as collateral. The ten supported networks include Solana, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Mantle, TON, Ink, X Layer, Arbitrum, Tron and Optimism. xStocks reports availability in more than 110 countries.
Economic Exposure Does Not Equal Share Ownership

The European Securities and Markets Authority classifies these structures as wrapped tokenised equities. In its latest risk report, ESMA said these tokens typically represent a claim on, or economic exposure to, shares held by a trusted party.

Legal ownership of the underlying securities remains offchain, so transferring a wrapped token does not necessarily transfer legal title to the shares. ESMA said this structure adds dependencies on the token issuer, platform and underlying custodian.

Kraken similarly states that xStocks do not provide voting rights or a legal claim against the company whose shares back the token. Economic benefits from dividends are reflected by increasing the holder’s balance of the corresponding token.

xStocks are issued by Jersey-registered Backed Assets (JE) Limited. Eligible clients outside the European Economic Area may receive them through Payward Digital Solutions, which is licensed by the Bermuda Monetary Authority.

In the EU and EEA, Payward Europe Digital Solutions offers them. The products are unavailable to residents of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and sanctioned jurisdictions. Access through individual exchanges and other integrations remains subject to local rules and partner eligibility checks.

title: Kraken's xStocks Backing Assets Top $800 Million as Holders Pass 300,000
